file_uploader with large file results in server getting killed

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I am using st.file_uploader to upload ~3.5gb file into my streamlit dashboard. This however, results in the server getting killed.
When I inspect using btop, Upon file upload, the server starts using an astronomic amount of RAM.

EDIT: I tried imposing a RAM limit by dockerizing the dashboard and settting a 4gb RAM limit, but it just gets killed in the container.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a video file", type=["mp4", "mov", "avi"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

streamlit run dashboard.py --maxUploadSize=5000

### Expected Behavior

It's probably better to stream it in chunks to disk when clicking an 'upload file' button.

### Current Behavior

The server gets killed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:


### Additional Information

_No response_

facts_with_quotes.quote:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome

### Summary

Watch discuss Topic:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/after-upload-file-stays-in-ram/119453/2

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

I tryed several solutions:

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

The phenomenon is:
If I set the clear_on_submit=false and deactivate the st.rerun() I am able to delete the File in the Widget and only then the file gets deleted from the RAM.

I tested it with a simple Upload code with the same result in different browsers on 2 different PCs and different streamlit versions.

Actually I have no idea how to fix this, can somebody help?

payload.message:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.


### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior : 

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

streamlit v 1.55

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Copy the 3 files
2. docker compose up (or, it's _really just_ python 3.10 and streamlit 1.55 in the env, nothing else)
3. Open browser to streamlit instance
4. Compare the browser logs, the python logs, and how the page doesn't load

### Expected Behavior

I expect at app start the component to fail, but afterwards I'd expect each new component creation to successfully be created, successfully transmit setState/TriggerValue back to the component, and get returned by the component, before the backend continues on. (Consistency / Determinism). (Otherwise, we'd design differently)

### Current Behavior

I've tried variations of the above files, such as adding more sleeps on python side, but the js side seems to be sending the values back, and the python side seems to inconsistently receive them. The first component ~1/2 the time, and the second always fails when the first doesn't.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.55
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Ubuntu
- Browser: Chromium / Opera

    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

For deferred download with `st.download_button`, pipe errors to the script thread

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, there should be a way to catch errors that may be raised by the deferred generation function. Currently, if the funciton encounters an error, a warning message is displayed on the frontend and isn't accessible on the backend.

### Why?

When you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, the function which returns the download runs on its own thread so it won't block the script thread. This has two consequences:
1. There is no script context, so you can't use any Streamlit command, like `st.session_state`. (See #13337).
2. You can't handle errors raised by the deferred download function.

You can put try-catch blocks in your download function to avoid an unhandled error, but you can't really _do_ anything about it because you can't display a custom message or log something in Session State. (Maybe you could hack a solution by writing something to a temporary file on the server, but that doesn't seem ideal.)

### How?

A couple different solutions:
* Have the download button return an error if encountered so it can be caught in the main script.
* Give the download thread some (possibly restricted) script context (like #13337).
* Improve multithreading support more generally, and have some hook at the end of a script run to catch a session's child threads, like the download thread.

### Additional Context

_No response_

payload.message:
st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

### Current Behavior

See steps to reproduce.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3a172ba-92e2-4ec7-bcea-6d1ec0fde7b9

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian 3.12 Trixie (Docker)
- Browser: Brave (Chrome) (Brave 1.83.118 / Chromium: 141.0.7390.108)


### Additional Information

I believe this is the same issue as #11160 but that issue author never responded.

Incomplete type hint for date_input max_value: missing Literal["today"]

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

It looks like the type hints for `st.date_input` are incomplete.

In `time_widgets.date_input`, the `max_value` parameter is typed as `SingleDateValue`, but the function also accepts the string literal `"today"`, as documented and supported at runtime.

This causes static type checkers (e.g. mypy, pyright, pylance) to raise errors even though the code is valid.

Suggested fix:
Extend the type hint to include Literal["today"]
This likely affects min_value as well.

Thanks!

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    max_value="today",
)
```

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column. As a result, text input in a cell of an empty column is stored in a list in the underlying pandas DataFrame. For example, entering `"my value"` results to `["my value"]` in the DataFrame cell. Even explicitly configuring the column as Text column with `st.column_config.TextColumn` does not work. The bug is introduced by the recent 1.52.0 release. I believe it's due to this change:
```
if column_data_kind in (ColumnDataKind.LIST, ColumnDataKind.EMPTY):
            return list(value) if is_list_like(value) else [value]  # ty: ignore 
```
From this merged PR:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12935/files

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame([{'a': None}])

modified_df = st.data_editor(df)

print(modified_df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Input "text" should set the text in the DataFrame cell, not a list. 

### Current Behavior

Currently, input "text" set ["text"] instead of "text" in the DataFrame cell. 

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1 and 1.52.0
- Python version: 3.13.2
- Operating System: Windows 
- Browser: Chrome 


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column. As a result, text input in a cell of an empty column is stored in a list in the underlying pandas DataFrame. For example, entering `"my value"` results to `["my value"]` in the DataFrame cell. Even explicitly configuring the column as Text column with `st.column_config.TextColumn` does not work. The bug is introduced by the recent 1.52.0 release. I believe it's due to this change:
```
if column_data_kind in (ColumnDataKind.LIST, ColumnDataKind.EMPTY):
            return list(value) if is_list_like(value) else [value]  # ty: ignore 
```
From this merged PR:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12935/files

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame([{'a': None}])

modified_df = st.data_editor(df)

print(modified_df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Input "text" should set the text in the DataFrame cell, not a list. 

### Current Behavior

Currently, input "text" set ["text"] instead of "text" in the DataFrame cell. 

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1 and 1.52.0
- Python version: 3.13.2
- Operating System: Windows 
- Browser: Chrome 


### Additional Information

_No response_

Add support for PyCapsule

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add support in Streamlit’s data APIs (e.g. st.dataframe, charts) for consuming objects that implement [Apache Arrow’s PyCapsule](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html) C data interface (via `__arrow_c_schema__`, `__arrow_c_array__`, `__arrow_c_stream__`, etc.), so that Arrow-compatible tables/streams from any library can be passed in without requiring a hard dependency on PyArrow or extra data copies. This would enable zero-copy interoperability with other Arrow-based ecosystems (including potential device-backed data via the device variants of these methods) and make Streamlit more future-proof as more Python libraries adopt this standardized Arrow PyCapsule protocol.

### Additional Context

- https://github.com/vega/altair/issues/3568#issue-2506363561
- https://github.com/narwhals-dev/narwhals/pull/1181
- https://github.com/microsoft/LightGBM/issues/6204#issuecomment-2256015538
- Comparison to Dataframe Interchange Protocol: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html#comparison-to-dataframe-interchange-protocol

def arrow_table_from_dfi_dataframe(dfi_df: DataFrameLike) -> pa.Table: 
     """Convert a DataFrame Interchange Protocol compatible object to an Arrow Table.""" 
     import pyarrow as pa 
  
     # First check if the dataframe object has a method to convert to arrow. 
     # Give this preference over the pyarrow from_dataframe function since the object 
     # has more control over the conversion, and may have broader compatibility. 
     # This is the case for Polars, which supports Date32 columns in direct conversion 
     # while pyarrow does not yet support this type in from_dataframe 
     for convert_method_name in ("arrow", "to_arrow", "to_arrow_table", "to_pyarrow"): 
         convert_method = getattr(dfi_df, convert_method_name, None) 
         if callable(convert_method): 
```

    # pa.table() will automatically check for `__arrow_c_stream__` and call that
    # todo: add pyarrow version check; I forget which version added support for the PyCapsule Interface
    return pa.table(dfi_df)
```

payload.message:
File upload fails on Android mobile browsers

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When trying to upload a PDF file, it fails, and instead shows "connecting" 1 second and gets back to initial state. 
This issue doesn't always happen, but in general, I need to re-attempt several times to make the upload work.
It happens even with small pdf files (<200kB)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Simple PDF Upload Test")

# File uploader for PDF files only
uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a PDF file", type=["pdf"])

if uploaded_file is not None:
    # Success message
    st.success(f"✅ File uploaded: **{uploaded_file.name}**")
    
    # Display file details
    st.write(f"**Size:** {uploaded_file.size:,} bytes")
    
    # Optional: Show file type and other metadata
    st.write(f"**MIME Type:** {uploaded_file.type}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Upload pdf file 

### Expected Behavior

File uploaded (works sometimes, after repeated attempts)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

Tap "Choose a PDF" → select file.
- **WebSocket drops instantly**.
- Server logs show **repeated connect/disconnect cycles**.

2025-10-31 09:36:32.729 DEBUG Received the following back message: rerun_script { ... }
2025-10-31 09:36:32.729 DEBUG Beginning script thread
2025-10-31 09:36:32.730 DEBUG Disconnecting files for session...
2025-10-31 09:36:32.730 DEBUG Runtime state: ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED
2025-10-31 09:36:40.831 DEBUG Runtime state: NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED
2025-10-31 09:36:47.998 DEBUG Runtime state: ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED

... (repeats rapidly during upload attempt)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit version**: `1.51.0`
- **Python version**: `3.12.3`
- **Operating system**: Ubuntu on **AWS EC2 t3.small**
- **Browsers**: 
- **Chrome on Android (mobile)** – Version 139.0.7258.62
- Firefox 141.0.1
- Lemur 2.7.3.013

Command: streamlit run test_upload.py --server.port=8501
Instance: AWS EC2 t3.small (2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM)
Network: Public IP, port 8501 open in security group
No reverse proxy, no Docker, no custom config
Client: Android Chrome 
File type: application/pdf → triggers disconnect


### Additional Information

_No response_

libodbc2 conflicts with preinstalled libodbc1 from Microsoft in Streamlit Cloud

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Trying to install `libodbc2` fails with the following message:

```
dpkg: error processing archive /tmp/apt-dpkg-install-NKXxq6/218-libodbc2_2.3.11-2+deb12u1_amd64.deb (--unpack):
 trying to overwrite '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libodbc.so.2.0.0', which is also in package libodbc1:amd64 2.3.11-3
```

This shouldn't happen since `libodbc1` should be just a transitional package depending on `libodbc2`, but this specific version comes from the Microsoft repositories and doesn't do that.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set up a github repository with any trivial, "Hello world"-like streamlit app.
2.  Add a `packages.txt` and put just `libodbc2` in it.
3. Try to deploy to Streamlit Cloud

The application is succesfully deployed.

Make three dots menu in `st.dataframe` keyboard accessible

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

The three dots menu in a header of `st.dataframe` is not keyboard accessible when tabbing through the app. It should be, regardless of whether the header is hovered or not. Note that we want to revisit best practices for this as part of a bigger accessibility push before fixing this. Some other popular datagrid libraries (e.g. AgGrid) do not expose this element for keyboard navigation since data grids already contain a lot of clickable elements.

payload.message:
Show top bar background only when needed (similar to ChatGPT)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

ChatGPT has a pretty nice UX for their top bar: If the window is wide enough to show the elements on the top left/right without blocking the page content, the top bar doesn't have a background. Only if they would overlap the page content, the top bar gets a white background (and a gray border). 

Maybe we should try something similar? Given that our top bar is very similar, with some things on the top left and top right but not much in between. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a194f1b9-6bd4-460f-a348-bd6165ccd008

### Why?

- Nicer UX. 
- More available screen height for the page content. 

### How?

Similar to ChatGPT but without the gray border. We'd definitely need to try this out to see if it feels good. Also need to see how this interacts with `st.navigation(..., position="top")`. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The example in https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe titled: "Example 2: Programmatically set selections" does not work if we try with empty selections.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from numpy.random import default_rng as rng

df = pd.DataFrame(rng(0).standard_normal((12, 5)), columns=["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"])

if st.button("Select the first row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [0], "columns": [], "cells": []}}
if st.button("Select no row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}

event = st.dataframe(
    df,
    key="data",
    on_select="rerun",
    selection_mode=["single-row"],
)

st.code(event.selection)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Select a row
3. Click on the button "Select the first row", it works as expected
4. Select a row again
5. Click on the button "Select no row", the dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection.

### Expected Behavior

The row selection should match the dataframe selection state and be empty.

### Current Behavior

The dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection and is not empty.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: WSL Docker
- Browser: Edge

Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python

summary.problem:
Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

worked when ran with
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.57.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
stopped working at
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.58.0 streamlit run repro.py
```

payload.message:
Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) for st.login() sessions

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add opt-in support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to the native authentication flow, so the _streamlit_user cookie set by st.login() becomes useless when copied off the device it was issued on.

Currently only Chrome takes advantage of this but I am happy to implement it and open a pull request
W3C draft: https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-dbsc/

### Why?

Since 1.42, st.login() stores the user's identity in a signed cookie with a 30-day lifetime. The cookie is HttpOnly and Secure, which is right, but there is no server-side session state: a cookie copied from a browser profile by malware or a colleague with the laptop works on any other machine until it expires, and st.logout() only clears the local copy. The app-level mitigations available today are shortening the session age in application code and re-checking an allowlist on every rerun. Neither stops a stolen cookie from being used within its window.

DBSC is the web platform's answer to exactly this. The browser generates a key pair in the device's secure hardware at login, and the server issues a short-lived cookie that the browser can only renew by signing a challenge with that key. A copied cookie expires within minutes and cannot be refreshed elsewhere. Chrome shipped it as generally available on Windows in Chrome 146 and is rolling it out on macOS in Chrome 147, and it is a W3C WebAppSec draft. Browsers without support ignore the header and keep working as today, so it degrades cleanly.

Streamlit apps are frequently internal dashboards with real data behind Google or Entra logins, which is the population this protects.

### How?

The change is contained in the Starlette auth layer and needs no frontend work. Sketch:

1. **Registration header.** In the OAuth callback, alongside the existing cookies, send `Secure-Session-Registration` pointing at a new route, with the supported algorithms (ES256, RS256).
2. **Two new routes** next to `/auth/login`, `/auth/logout` and `/auth/callback`:
   - `/auth/dbsc/register`: verifies the browser's signed registration JWT, records the device public key, returns the session config, and sets a short-lived `__Host-` bound cookie.
   - `/auth/dbsc/refresh`: on a missing or expired bound cookie the browser calls this with a signed challenge; the server verifies it against the registered key and reissues the bound cookie.
3. **Stateless key storage.** Streamlit has no server-side session store and runs as one process, so rather than adding one, the device key's thumbprint is written into the existing signed `_streamlit_user` cookie at registration. Refresh verifies the challenge signature against the thumbprint carried in the cookie. Restarts and multiple replicas are then unaffected, matching how the current cookie works.
4. **Websocket check.** The `/_stcore/stream` endpoint, which already decodes the identity cookie on connect, refuses a connection whose identity cookie is bound but whose bound cookie is absent.
5. **Configuration.** A new `[auth]` option, off by default, for example `device_bound_sessions = true`. Requires HTTPS, since `__Host-` cookies are refused otherwise, which is already true of production `st.login()` deployments.

Signature verification can use authlib's JOSE support, which is already a dependency of the auth feature.

One point to verify during implementation: Chrome defers ordinary requests while it refreshes an expired bound cookie, and the behaviour for a WebSocket upgrade is not spelled out in the spec. The frontend fetches `/_stcore/host-config` and `/_stcore/health` over HTTP before opening the stream, which should trigger the refresh first, but this needs a real-browser test.


### Additional Context

- Chrome for Developers, DBSC overview and server integration: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/device-bound-session-credentials
- Chrome 147 macOS rollout: https://scotthelme.co.uk/device-bound-session-credentials-lands-in-chrome-on-macos/

### Checklist

### Summary
The hover toolbar that `st.dataframe` draws (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen)
renders each button at 22.4 x 22.4 CSS px, and the buttons sit next to each other, so axe-core's
`target-size` rule (impact: serious, WCAG 2.2 AA, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)) fails. Cause:

st.map - autodetection of lat/long columns picks one out of the list

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi, 

stumbled across the ambiguity of the detecting of the geo columns for st.map.

*current behavior*: When users do not specify coordinate column, st.map looks for following columns: 
`_DEFAULT_LAT_COL_NAMES: Final = {"lat", "latitude", "LAT", "LATITUDE"}
_DEFAULT_LON_COL_NAMES: Final = {"lon", "longitude", "LON", "LONGITUDE"}
`
.

Apparently, if the dataframe contains more than one of those columns, st.map picks one of them.
This leads to different views per run, it can mix combinations. 

Expectation would be that there is a warning / error in this case , instead of silently accepting the input.

`import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# Sample DataFrame with latitude, longitude, color, and size columns
data = {
    "latitude": [34.0522, 37.7749, 40.7128],
    "longitude": [-118.2437, -122.4194, -74.0060],
    "lat": [0, 0, 0],
    "lon": [-0, 0, 0],
    "size": [10, 20, 15],
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
st.map(df)
`

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

# Sample DataFrame with latitude, longitude, color, and size columns

    "lat": [0, 0, 0],

}

st.map(df)
```

Clarify st.number_input return type when value= int | None

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Passing a typed variable of int | None to the value parameter for number_input returns a float | None type.

I expected this to be int | None, and that this is how you are expected to create an empty input field, that accepts integers only, assuming the step parameter would default to 1, but it appears that strictly requires value to be int.

If you set step=1, then static type checking works as expected, resolving to int | None.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

default_value: int | None = None

number = st.number_input(
    "Input number",
    value=default_value,
)

if number:
    assert isinstance(number, int)
    print('Number is an int')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run example
2. Input number

### Expected Behavior

Prints 'Number is an int'

### Current Behavior

Assertion fails.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Edge


### Additional Information

summary.problem:
Clarify st.number_input return type when value= int | None

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Passing a typed variable of int | None to the value parameter for number_input returns a float | None type.

I expected this to be int | None, and that this is how you are expected to create an empty input field, that accepts integers only, assuming the step parameter would default to 1, but it appears that strictly requires value to be int.

If you set step=1, then static type checking works as expected, resolving to int | None.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

default_value: int | None = None

number = st.number_input(
    "Input number",
    value=default_value,
)

if number:
    assert isinstance(number, int)
    print('Number is an int')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run example
2. Input number

### Expected Behavior

Prints 'Number is an int'

### Current Behavior

Assertion fails.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Edge

_No response_

payload.message:
Frontend uses user-controlled file name as FormData field name in file upload

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `uploadFileUploaderFile`, the frontend constructs a `FormData` object for file uploads using the file's own name (`name`) as the multipart form-data field name: `form.append(name, file, fileName)`. Because the backend does not rely on this dynamic field name and files are uploaded individually, using the user-controlled filename introduces potential security risks, such as bypassing security filters, WAFs, or length restrictions designed for form field names.


```typescript
const form = new FormData()
const { name, webkitRelativePath } = file
// For directory uploads, use the relative path as fileName to preserve directory structure
const fileName = webkitRelativePath || name
form.append(name, file, fileName)

```

### Proposed Solution

Replace the dynamic `name` variable with a static string (such as `"file"`), since files are handled individually and the backend does not require the field name to match the filename.

```typescript
const form = new FormData()
const { name, webkitRelativePath } = file
// For directory uploads, use the relative path as fileName to preserve directory structure
const fileName = webkitRelativePath || name
form.append("file", file, fileName)

```


### Security Impact

* **User-Controlled Field Names:** Attackers can manipulate file names (including special characters, injection sequences, or excessive lengths) which are then directly injected into the multipart form-data structure as the field name.
* **Validation & WAF Bypasses:** Backend proxies, Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), or API gateways often enforce strict validation rules (character sets, maximum length) on form field names. Allowing client-side filenames to define these keys can lead to unexpected parsing behavior or security filter evasion.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file")
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.write(f"Uploaded filename: {uploaded_file.name}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the provided Python script using Streamlit.
2. Open your browser's Developer Tools and navigate to the **Network** tab.
3. Upload a file via the file uploader (e.g., a file named `malicious_name_test.txt`).
4. Inspect the multipart `form-data` payload sent in the upload request.
5. Observe that the form field `name` attribute equals the file's name (`malicious_name_test.txt`) instead of a static, controlled identifier.

### Expected Behavior

The multipart form-data request should use a static, predefined field name (such as `name="file"`) for the upload payload, ensuring that the form field name is fully controlled and sanitized, while the actual file name/path remains properly preserved only in the filename parameter.

### Current Behavior

When a file is uploaded through `st.file_uploader`, the frontend dynamically sets the multipart form-data field name to match the uploaded file's name (`form.append(name, file, fileName)`). As a result, user-controlled strings, special characters, and arbitrary lengths are directly injected into the request's form field name.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
Frontend uses user-controlled file name as FormData field name in file upload

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `uploadFileUploaderFile`, the frontend constructs a `FormData` object for file uploads using the file's own name (`name`) as the multipart form-data field name: `form.append(name, file, fileName)`. Because the backend does not rely on this dynamic field name and files are uploaded individually, using the user-controlled filename introduces potential security risks, such as bypassing security filters, WAFs, or length restrictions designed for form field names.


```typescript
const form = new FormData()
const { name, webkitRelativePath } = file
// For directory uploads, use the relative path as fileName to preserve directory structure
const fileName = webkitRelativePath || name
form.append(name, file, fileName)

```

### Proposed Solution

Replace the dynamic `name` variable with a static string (such as `"file"`), since files are handled individually and the backend does not require the field name to match the filename.

```typescript
const form = new FormData()
const { name, webkitRelativePath } = file
// For directory uploads, use the relative path as fileName to preserve directory structure
const fileName = webkitRelativePath || name
form.append("file", file, fileName)

```


### Security Impact

* **User-Controlled Field Names:** Attackers can manipulate file names (including special characters, injection sequences, or excessive lengths) which are then directly injected into the multipart form-data structure as the field name.
* **Validation & WAF Bypasses:** Backend proxies, Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), or API gateways often enforce strict validation rules (character sets, maximum length) on form field names. Allowing client-side filenames to define these keys can lead to unexpected parsing behavior or security filter evasion.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file")
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.write(f"Uploaded filename: {uploaded_file.name}")
```

1. Run the provided Python script using Streamlit.
2. Open your browser's Developer Tools and navigate to the **Network** tab.
3. Upload a file

payload.message:
st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header

### Summary

The media endpoint that serves `st.download_button` files builds its `Content-Disposition` header by interpolating the download filename into a quoted string, `filename="{filename}"`, whenever the name is latin-1 encodable. A double quote is latin-1 encodable, so any filename containing one closes the quoted parameter early and the rest of the name spills out as trailing tokens. The emitted header is not valid per RFC 6266, and the name the browser saves the file under is no longer the name the app set.

This needs nothing adversarial to hit. An ordinary filename like `5" x 7" print.jpg` (inch marks) is enough. The name reaches this sink from `st.download_button(file_name=...)`, and since 1.61.0 also from the filename inferred off an uploaded file when `file_name` is omitted.

The safe branch already exists in the same function: a name that is not latin-1 encodable takes `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}`, which percent-encodes and cannot break out. The bug is only which branch a name reaches. Streamlit's own dependency, Starlette, makes the correct choice for the same header in `FileResponse` (`starlette/responses.py`), selecting the quoted form only when `quote(filename) == filename`.

### Reproducible Code Example

Fully in-process against the real media route, no browser needed:

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.testclient import TestClient
from streamlit.runtime.media_file_storage import MediaFileKind
from streamlit.runtime.memory_media_file_storage import MemoryMediaFileStorage
from streamlit.web.server.starlette.starlette_routes import create_media_routes

# An ordinary filename: a 5 inch by 7 inch print. The inch marks are
# double quotes, which are perfectly valid in a filename.
filename = '5" x 7" print.jpg'

storage = MemoryMediaFileStorage("/media")
file_id = storage.load_and_get_id(
    b"jpeg-bytes", "image/jpeg", MediaFileKind.DOWNLOADABLE, filename
)
client = TestClient(Starlette(routes=create_media_routes(storage, "")))
response = client.get(storage.get_url(file_id))
print(response.headers["content-disposition"])
```

The same header is produced end to end from an app, without touching internals:

```python
import streamlit as st

uploaded = st.file_uploader("upload")
if uploaded:
    # The inch marks in the file_name break the emitted header.
    st.download_button("download", data=uploaded, file_name='5" x 7" print.jpg')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `pip install streamlit==1.61.1`
2. Save the first snippet above as `repro.py`.
3. Run `python repro.py`.
4. Observe the printed header: `attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"`. The `filename` parameter is terminated by the first `"` after `5`, so the value a conforming parser reads is not the name the app set.

### Expected Behavior

A filename with characters that are not safe unescaped inside a quoted string (a double quote, a semicolon, a space) should still be carried faithfully in a valid header, using the RFC 5987 `filename*=` form, exactly as the non-latin-1 branch already does and as Starlette's `FileResponse` does:

```
attachment; filename*=utf-8''5%22%20x%207%22%20print.jpg
```

### Current Behavior

The name is interpolated into `filename="..."` verbatim, so the double quote closes the parameter:

```
attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"
```

That is not a valid RFC 6266 header: the quoted string ends at the first unescaped `"`, and everything after it is stray tokens. A name that also contains `;` can introduce additional `Content-Disposition` parameters, so the header's structure ends up controlled by the filename rather than by Streamlit.

Root cause, `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py` in `_media_endpoint`:

```python
try:
    filename.encode("latin1")
    disposition = f'filename="{filename}"'
except UnicodeEncodeError:
    disposition = f"filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}"
headers["Content-Disposition"] = f"attachment; {disposition}"
```

The branch is selected on latin-1 encodability, but the property that matters is whether the value is safe unescaped inside a quoted parameter, and `"`, `;` and space are all latin-1 encodable.

### Fix direction

Select the branch the way Starlette's `FileResponse` does in `starlette/responses.py`: emit the plain `filename="..."` form only when `quote(filename) == filename`, and fall back to `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}` otherwise. This is a strict superset of the current safe branch (every non-latin-1 name still percent-encodes) and additionally routes latin-1 names that need escaping onto the safe form. Plain ASCII names like `report.pdf` keep the quoted form unchanged.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1 (present since 1.60.0; also on current `develop`)
- Python version: 3.10 - 3.14
- Operating System: any
- Browser: n/a (backend header construction; the visible effect is the saved download name)

payload.message:
Periodic server-driven data refresh shared across sessions (vs. per-session run_every)

## Summary

Provide a way to refresh a data source on a **server-side schedule** — computed
once for the whole app and pushed to every session currently viewing it —
instead of each session running its own `run_every` timer and recomputing the
same query independently. This is the shared "the dashboard refreshes every
minute and everyone sees the latest" pattern that live/ops dashboards need.

## Why?

`@st.fragment(run_every=…)` already gives time-driven updates, but the timer and
the computation are **per session**: with _N_ viewers on the same dashboard you
get _N_ timers and _N_ executions of the same query every interval. A refresh
that is cheap for one user becomes _N×_ load on the warehouse/API for a shared
internal tool.

`@st.cache_data` dedupes the *computation* across sessions, but nothing *drives*
a periodic refresh or *wakes* the sessions when a new value lands — today
`run_every` is the driver, and it's per session. The missing piece is a refresh
that runs once for the whole app and updates every session viewing it.

## How?

Mark a cached data source to refresh on a fixed interval, centrally for the
whole app. Any fragment that reads it shows the current value and re-renders when
a new one lands.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
# The value refreshes centrally every 60s; sessions read the current value and
# rerun when a new one lands — no per-session timer, one shared computation.
@st.cache_data(refresh_every="60s")
def latest_metrics():
    return run_warehouse_query()

@st.fragment
def kpis():
    df = latest_metrics()          # returns the current cached value immediately
    st.metric("Orders", len(df))
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

kpis()
```

## Additional Context

- Split out from [#12980](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12980)
  ("real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script"), which is being
  closed now that fragments (`run_every`), `st.rerun(scope=…)`, and element
  diffing cover the original per-session/live-update and flicker concerns.
- Related in-flight work: the non-blocking background execution spec
  ([#17067](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17067)) covers shared,
  off-thread cached computation; scheduled/recurring refresh is called out there
  as not-yet-built.
- Companion gap: a **freshness signal**
  ([#17141](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17141)) — a cheap "did
  the source change?" probe (e.g. Snowflake change-tracking / `LAST_ALTERED` /
  `MAX(updated_at)`) to drive **event-driven** invalidation instead of a blind
  timer. That's the push counterpart to this timer-based one.

payload.message:
Add to cache decorators last time of cached.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the cache decorators are just simple decorators of a hashable saving with the possibility of clearing the cache.

However, a key component in caching is when the cache was saved.

Currently the only method to now this is by caching the result with a timestamp, which is unpractical.

So I'm thinking about a ´´´cached_function.time()´´´ method for knowing when it was last cached.

### Why?

Because knowing the time of the cache would be very comprehensive for:
- Not clearing cache everytime an update is needed, checking first if the time of the cache is soon enough
- Simply adding a display of Last Updated at

### How?

When saving the cache save the timestamp as well and implement a .time method to the cached function for retrieving the time as a time.time() timestamp.

### Additional Context

_No response_

payload.message:
Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

- Visually aligns `st.tabs` with the existing pill styling used by `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`, but with the `st.tabs` container model.
- Design references for the pills style:
  - [Tailwind Plus — Tabs (pill variant)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/navigation/tabs#component-2a66fc822e8ad55f59321825e5af0980)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, solid variant](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-tabs-solid-variant)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, stretched](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-streched-tabs)

Luminosity contrast ratio of link icon is 1.162:1 which is less than required ratio 3:1 in windows.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Luminosity contrast ratio of link icon is 1.162:1 which is less than required ratio 3:1 in windows. Low vision users will be impacted as the link icon appears faint and hard to notice due to poor contrast. payload.message:
Feature: st.scatterplot_matrix_chart — scatterplot matrix (SPLOM) navigation with excentric labeling and lasso query layers

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

## Summary

Add `st.scatterplot_matrix_chart`, a native chart command for exploring multivariate/high-dimensional tabular data through a scatterplot matrix (SPLOM). It adds animated "rolling" navigation between attribute pairs, excentric labeling for dense regions, and persistent lasso-based query layers that let you track a subset of rows across different attribute views.

## Why?

Data scientists frequently need to explore relationships across many numeric columns at once. A standard SPLOM grid gives a good overview, but it's hard to inspect any one pair in detail, label individual points in dense clusters, or keep track of the same subset of rows as you move between attribute pairs. This is a longstanding, well-studied interaction pattern in the information-visualization literature, and I think it's a good fit for Streamlit's data-science audience:

- I first built a version of this technique in a data visualization course project over a decade ago (~2012), based on:
  - Pierre Dragicevic ([USER]) et al., "Rolling the Dice: Multidimensional Visual Exploration using Scatterplot Matrix Navigation"
  - Jean-Daniel Fekete ([USER]) and Catherine Plaisant, "Excentric Labeling: Dynamic Neighborhood Labeling for Data Visualization"
  - My original project instructions/write-up from that time (personal notes, kept private)
- A few years ago, a tech company I was working with asked me to use Streamlit, and separately took an interest in this old scatterplot project of mine. Looking back, I read that as an implicit nudge toward combining the two — bringing this navigation technique into Streamlit itself, rather than leaving it as a standalone tool.

Revisiting both experiences, I think this technique deserves a first-class home in Streamlit rather than living on as scattered internal/academic tools.

## How?

I generalized the navigation technique above into a self-contained, WebGL-rendered element and exposed it as a new command, `st.scatterplot_matrix_chart`:

- A small scatterplot cell for every pair of chosen numeric columns, plus one large "detail" plot.
- Left-click a cell to jump to it; right-click (or arrow keys) to "roll" to it through an animated transition across intermediate cells.
- Hover the large plot for an excentric label lens (labels fan out around the cursor in dense regions).
- Up to 8 independent, colored query layers: lasso-select points in the large plot to build a persistent subset, then navigate to other attribute pairs to see how that same subset behaves elsewhere.
- Selections are returned to Python via `on_select="rerun"` as row indices, so they can drive the rest of the app.

A full implementation (backend + frontend + tests) is up for review at #16059.

## Additional Context

- Original ~2012 project instructions (background/inspiration, written by me as a student at the time — personal notes, kept private)
- Academic references: Dragicevic et al., "Rolling the Dice: Multidimensional Visual Exploration using Scatterplot Matrix Navigation"; Fekete & Plaisant, "Excentric Labeling: Dynamic Neighborhood Labeling for Data Visualization"
- Implementation PR: #16059
